target.user-input: the browser app talks to the Rust engine behind one switch, and glyph-ui.js changes only at its transport

constraint.user-input: the protocol is ADR B: the page posts one request line to /engine on its own origin, and serve-dev.js relays it to glyph-engine with --engine rust, or to glyph-protocol.js
the transport is a Core of the same shape as GlyphCore: the twelve calls go through /engine, and the tables, esc, xesc and walk stay the JS core

note.user-input: run is synchronous: the transport asks with a synchronous request, the one reading that leaves glyph-ui.js untouched; question 9 of the return stays open for the Regent
parse cannot send the live tree: the transport rebuilds segments from the full envelope, and buildXml and serializeAST ask toXML and toAST of the source the segments came from
the engine answers with the repository stores; the templates a page merges stay on the JS path, as question 11 of the return reads it

instruction.user-input: the switch is one query parameter of the page, engine=relay; without it the page runs on the JS core as it does today

validate.user-input: the app on the Rust engine
the app drives the 114 sources through Rust with the same bytes as through JS, and the JS path still works
